the preparation of the glucose biosensor using carbon nanotubes and IO(4)-oxidized GOx, which has the advantage that the biosensor is fabricated without any cross-linking reagent.
the development of a novel glucose biosensor based on IO4-oxidation of glucose oxidase and covalent self-assembled layer-by-layer deposition of the enzyme on the amino terminated carbon nanotubes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the glucose sensor constructed by AMWNTs/IO4-oxidize GOx showed excellent electrocatalytic performance toward the reduction of dissolved O2, and the analytical performances of the glucose sensor could be tuned by the number of GOX/AMWNT bilayers.
the glucose biosensors prepared using the LBL method with the AMWNTs showed excellent electrocatalytic activity toward glucose and good reproducibility and repeatability.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glucose biosensors based on the GOx/AMNTs bilayer films were fabricated by the simple and efficient covalent LBL self-assembly method.
the glucose biosensor with 5 GOx/AMWTs bilayers exhibited a high sensitivity of 0.25 mA mM-1 and a detection limit as low as 0.2 mM for glucose.
the glucose biosensor based on IO4-oxidzed GOx/AMWNt could be a good alternative to the glucose biosensor with GOx immobilized on the surface of carbon nanotubes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AMWNTs are useful for constructing enzyme electrodes, which are stable and can be easily operated at a low potential.
the use of MWNTs functionalized with amino group is a facile and effective approach to fabricate glucose biosensors with improved analytical performance.
the LBL self-assembly method can be used to fabricate glucose biosensors using GOx and AMWNTs.
